stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
The full subcategory $\text{Ac}$ of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$
consisting of acyclic modules is a strictly full saturated triangulated
subcategory of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$.
The corresponding saturated multiplicative system

of $K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})$ is the class $\text{Qis}$
of quasi-isomorphisms. In particular, the kernel of the localization
functor
$$
Q : K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}) \to
\text{Qis}^{-1}K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})
$$
is $\text{Ac}$. Moreover, the functor $H^0$ factors through $Q$.
hypotheses: (A,d) is a dg algebra; consider its dg-module homotopy category.
conclusions: Acyclic dg A-modules form a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory Ac; quasi-isomorphisms form the associated saturated multiplicative system, the kernel of localization Q is Ac, and H⁰ factors through Q.

reason: The cohomological functor H^0 and shifts detect precisely acyclic dg modules and quasi-isomorphisms, so the cited general derived localization lemma identifies the saturated triangulated kernel and localization class. The source also addresses set-theoretic size by partial universes and forthcoming property-(P) mapping computations.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $D(A, \text{d})$ has both direct sums and products,
\item direct sums are obtained by taking direct sums of differential graded
modules,
\item products are obtained by taking products of differential
graded modules.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
conclusions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $D(A, \text{d})$ has both direct sums and products,
\item direct sums are obtained by taking direct sums of differential graded
modules,
\item products are obtained by taking products of differential
graded modules.
\end{enumerate}

reason: Using property-(I) resolutions of codomains, the derived Hom out of an ordinary direct sum decomposes as a product, verifying its coproduct universal property. With property-(P) resolutions of domains, derived Hom into ordinary dg products similarly decomposes as a product, verifying product universality. The last sentence incorrectly says 'direct sums' instead of 'products' but the calculation is clear.
